::J U D G M E N T:

: 
The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondent under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-
with interest for the death of Sri. K.M. Munikrishnappa in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 30.04.2023.

2. The case of the petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 30.04.2023 at about 12.20 p.m., when the deceased was riding the Motor bike bearing Reg. No.KA-40- EA-5896 on left side of Vijayapura - Chikkaballapur Road, near Kommasandra, Devanahalli Taluk, at that time, the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D-4109 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and SCCH-10 dashed to the deceased, as a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
The petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are sons of the deceased.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 54 years and he was doing Coolie work and agriculture and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.
The respondent being owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this claim petition.
3. After presentation of the petition, notice was issued to the respondent.
Though the respondent has appeared before the Court, despite giving sufficient opportunity he has failed to file written statement.

4. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
SCCH-10 5.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following points arise for my determination :

sentences.text: POINTS

1) Whether the petitioners proved that, Sri. K.M. Munikrishnappa succumbed to the fatal injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 30.04.2023 at about 12.20 p.m., on Vijayapura - Chikkaballapur Road, near Kommasandra, Devanahalli Taluk, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D-4109 ?
2) Whether the petitioners proved that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri. K.M.
Munikrishnappa ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for? If yes, for what quantum ?
4) What order or award?

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
7.

My finding on the above points are as follows:
SCCH-10 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : In the Affirmative Point No.3 :

R E A S O N S 8. POINT No.1:
The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of death of Sri. K.M. Munikrishnappa in the road traffic accident.
9.
The petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and examined herself as PW-1.
On behalf of the petitioners, 14 documents were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0079/2023 of Vijayapura police and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the offending Canter Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D-4109.

Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet filed by the Vijayapura police against accused No.1 i.e. one Mr. Irfan Pasha who is none other than the driver of the offending SCCH-10 vehicle and accused No.2 / respondent for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 304-A of IPC and Sec. 146 and 196 of Motor Vehicles Act.
On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
10. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.

deceased died due to head injury and intra cranial hemorrhage.

Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the SCCH-10 accident in question had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D-4109 and deceased Sri. K.M. Munikrishnappa died in the alleged accident.
Hence, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
11. POINT No.2:-
It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased and they are depending on the deceased.
In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners have produced the copies of Aadhaar cards as per Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.14.

In the instant case,
though the respondent has appeared before the Court through his counsel, but not filed the written statement and not contested the petition and there is no dispute regarding the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly I answer Point No.2 in the Affirmative.
SCCH-10 12. POINT No.3:

It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, deceased K.M. Munikrishnappa was hale and healthy at the time of accident and was doing Coolie work and agriculture and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to untimely death of deceased they were put to great hardship.
13. Further to prove the occupation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Therefore, notional income has to be taken for consideration.
14. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the SCCH-10 notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, if the accident occurred in the year 2022 the notional income has to be taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that,
if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the deceased would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 30.04.2023.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the deceased.

Before proceeding to award compensation under the different heads, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.

sentences.text: Hon'ble

Apex Court in para No.61 has proceeded to record the following conclusions;
(iv) In case the deceased was self- SCCH-10 employed or on fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.

(v) For determination of the multiplicand, the deduction for personal and living expenses, the tribunals and the courts shall be guided by paragraphs 30 to 32 of Sarla Verma which we have reproduced hereinbefore.

(vi) The selection of multiplier shall be as indicated in the Table in Sarla Verma read with paragraph 42 of that judgment.
(vii) The age of the deceased should be the basis for applying the multiplier.
(viii) Reasonable figures on conventional head, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
16. To prove the age of the deceased, the petitioners have produced copy of Aadhaar card as per Ex-P14, wherein the SCCH-10 date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.06.1969.
The accident was occurred on 30.04.2023.
Therefore, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 54 years.

As per the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 an operative multiplier of 11 is applicable for the age group of 51 to 55 years.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors Vs. Delhi Transport Corp. and Anr reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. In the instant case, the deceased left behind his wife and sons and they are the dependents of the deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment reported in 2020 ACJ 759 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Birender & Others

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Birender & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, held that it must necessarily follow that, even the major,
married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representatives were fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim SCCH-10 towards conventional heads only.
18. In Sarla Verma case, the Hon'ble Apex Court has expressed the view regarding standardized deduction towards personal and living expenses.
where the number of dependents are 2 to 3, the deduction would be 1/3rd.

As discussed supra, in the present case, petitioners are the wife and sons Saraswathamma vs Waseem Khan on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81977385/
5 and they are the dependents.
Hence, in the present case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
In the present case, the Court has taken the view that the deceased was having monthly income of Rs.16,000/- (by relying on KSLSA notional income chart) and annual income would be Rs.1,92,000/-.

If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses,
the contribution to the family (dependents) is determined as Rs.1,28,000/-.
19.
In the present case, the deceased was aged 54 years at the time of accident and he was self employed.
Hence, an addition 10% is warranted towards future prospects.
If 10% SCCH-10 is added to the personal income of the deceased, it would be Rs.1,40,800/-.
The multiplier will be 11 having regard to the age of the deceased at the time of death (54 years).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.1,40,800/- X 11 = Rs.15,48,800/-.
Thus, Rs.15,48,800/- is the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

20. As per Pranay Sethi Case, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years from the date of judgment (31.10.2017).
Therefore, in the instant case, the petitioners are entitled for the aforesaid conventional heads with enhanced rate of 20%.

21. In Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Ors., (Civil Appeal No.9581/2018), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the children are entitled for parental consortium.

sentences.text: SCCH-10 22

. As discussed above, since Loss of estate, Loss of Consortium and Funeral expenses has been fixed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi Case, the petitioners are entitled to receive Rs.18,000/-, Rs.48,000/-each (petitioner No.1 to 3) and Rs.18,000/- respectively for loss of Estate,
consortium and funeral expenses.

23. From the above discussions the petitioner and brother of the petitioner are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Compensation  No.
 1) Loss of dependency Rs.15,48,800/-
 2) Loss of Consortium to Rs. 48,000/-
 petitioner No.1  3) Loss of Parental consortium Rs. 96,000/-
 (Rs.48,000 x 2 )
 4) Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000/-

As far as liability is concerned, in the instant case, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, as per the police records, the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.

Therefore, the respondent being owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D- 4109 is liable to pay compensation of Rs.17,28,800/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till its realization in the ratio of 60:20:20 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer the Point No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
25. Point No.4:

In view of my finding on Point No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner No.1 to 3 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,28,800/-(Rupees Seventeen Lakh SCCH-10 Twenty Thousand Eight hundred only) with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioners are entitled to receive compensation in the ratio of 60:20:20 respectively.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days from the date of this order.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount of petitioners shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioners through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.

Therefore, the respondent being owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-D- 4109 is liable to pay compensation of Rs.17,28,800/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till its realization in the ratio of 60:20:20 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer the Point No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.

In view of my finding on Point No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner No.1 to 3 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,28,800/-(Rupees Seventeen Lakh SCCH-10 Twenty Thousand Eight hundred only) with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
Petitioners are entitled to receive compensation in the ratio of 60:20:20 respectively.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days from the date of this order.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount of petitioners shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioners through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
